title: The end-of-year OSCE
intro: The Objective Structured Clinical Examination: two stations, eight minutes each, a buzzer between them. Examiners watch from the corner with a checklist. Read the door card, knock, and begin.

steps.say: A buzzer. Door card, station 1: Ms. Aisha Rahman, 38, "headache". Take a focused history and examination, then tell the examiner your plan.

choice.prompt: Ms. Rahman is holding her head in the dim room. You begin:

options.text: "Hello, I'm a medical student. I'm sorry you're in pain. Can you tell me about this headache?" Then you ask whether she'd like the lights left low.
options.reply: "Please. Thank you." The examiner ticks a box.

options.text: "On a scale of one to ten, how bad is your pain?"
options.reply: "Ten." Now what? You've skipped the introduction.

options.text: Switch the main light on so you can see her properly.
options.reply: She flinches from the light. The examiner writes something.

choice.lesson: Introduce yourself and attend to comfort; photophobia is a clue

history.opening: "It hit me like a bat to the back of the head. The worst headache of my life."

items.ask: How quickly did it come on?
items.answer: "Instantly. It was at its worst within a few seconds, at the gym, lifting."

items.ask: Have you ever had a headache like this before?
items.answer: "I get migraines, but nothing like this. This is the worst ever."

items.ask: Did you pass out, or have a seizure?
items.answer: "I think I blacked out for a second. My friend said I went pale."

items.ask: Any neck stiffness, or does light bother you?
items.answer: "My neck feels stiff. And the light hurts."

items.ask: Do you take blood thinners, or have high blood pressure?
items.answer: "No blood thinners. My blood pressure's always been fine."

items.ask: Anyone in the family had a brain aneurysm or kidney cysts?
items.answer: "My aunt died of a bleed in the brain."

items.ask: Do you smoke or use any drugs?
items.answer: "I smoke a few a day. No drugs."

maneuvers.name: Check for neck stiffness
maneuvers.finding: Neck flexion is stiff and painful.

steps.say: The buzzer. Door card, station 2: Mr. Samuel Otieno, 55, newly diagnosed with type 2 diabetes. His doctor has prescribed metformin. Explain it to him.

choice.prompt: How do you explain how to take it?

options.text: "You'll start with one tablet a day with your evening meal, and we'll increase it slowly over a few weeks. That helps your stomach get used to it."
options.reply: "With food, and slowly. That makes sense."

options.text: "Take the full dose on an empty stomach, twice a day."
options.reply: He frowns. The examiner frowns more.

options.text: "Just follow what the pharmacist's label says."
options.reply: "I was hoping you'd explain it," he says.

steps.question: osce_metformin_sick_01
steps.lead: "And if I get a stomach bug?"

choice.prompt: You have one minute left. How do you check he's understood?

options.text: "I've given you a lot of information. So I know I've explained it well, could you tell me in your own words how you'll take it?"
options.reply: He explains it back perfectly. The examiner nods.
"Yes," he says, as nearly everyone does.
He folds it into his pocket.

choice.lesson: Use teach-back: ask patients to explain the plan in their own words

steps.say: The final buzzer. You walk out into the corridor with the rest of your class, and for the first time in a year, nobody talks about the exam.

feedback: Examiner's comment: "Clear, safe and kind. Pass with distinction."
Examiner's comment: "Below the standard today. Your advisor will go through the recording with you, and you'll practice these stations again before second year."
